objective: Measure an approved event based service level objective and remaining error budget from scoped application request evidence, without treating missing telemetry as successful requests.

inputs.name: approved_scope
inputs.description: $SUB is the approved subscription GUID, $WORKSPACE is an approved Log Analytics workspace GUID and $APP_ID is the exact Application Insights resource ID in that subscription. $START and $END are ISO UTC timestamps. Validate resource ID characters and scope before KQL interpolation; reject quotes, backslashes and control characters.

inputs.name: slo_definition
inputs.description: Customer approved event eligibility, success definition, exclusions, observation window and target strictly between zero and one. HTTP success alone is not automatically the business success definition.

inputs.name: normalized_evidence
inputs.description: $INPUT is an operator prepared JSON file using the bundled synthetic references/evidence-example.json and shared operational-evidence.md contract. It contains total_events, good_events and unknown_events, evidence references, explicit scope and completeness. Sample values and thresholds must be replaced, not treated as production defaults.

permissions.role: Log Analytics Reader or equivalent approved query permission
permissions.scope: Only the approved workspace and scoped application evidence
permissions.purpose: Query application request telemetry without exporting user IDs, IP addresses or request bodies

collection.name: Read scoped request counts with sampling weights
collection.command:
$KQL = "AppRequests | where TimeGenerated >= datetime($START) and TimeGenerated < datetime($END) | where _ResourceId =~ '$APP_ID' | summarize total_events=sum(ItemCount), good_events=sumif(ItemCount, Success == true), unknown_events=sumif(ItemCount, isnull(Success))"
az monitor log-analytics query --subscription $SUB --workspace $WORKSPACE --analytics-query $KQL --timespan "$START/$END" --output json
collection.explanation: This executable query implements the simple technical request success definition only. Apply the approved eligibility and success predicate before production use. AppRequests ItemCount supplies sampling weights; do not use count() as an unsampled request total. Keep the raw query response privately and normalize its numeric cells to the documented input. An empty response, missing ItemCount, unknown Success, query cap or access denial is not zero failures. Record sampling and ingestion caveats.

collection.name: Analyze the approved normalized evidence locally
collection.command: python tools/operational_analysis.py --scenario slo-error-budget-analysis --input $INPUT --contract references/output-contract.json --output slo-private-result.json --sharing-output slo-sharing-draft.json
collection.explanation: Run from the deployed skill root, or a packaging-equivalent local bundle. All files are local. The shared tool performs no cloud calls. See [input and algorithm contract](./operational-evidence.md) and [synthetic example](./evidence-example.json). The private result satisfies the evidence contract; the sanitized sharing draft intentionally aliases identifiers and is not a replacement for private evidence.

analysis: Require a positive eligible event denominator, classified success evidence, explicit UTC window and customer target. Zero traffic and unknown success values are Not assessed.

Calculate SLI = good_events / total_events. Bad events = total_events minus good_events. Allowed bad events = total_events times (1 minus target). Retain fractional allowance and negative remaining budget rather than rounding away a breach.

Calculate remaining budget = allowed bad events minus bad events, and consumed ratio = bad events / allowed bad events. Compare the event based SLI with the approved target. Do not call this elapsed downtime or a contractual SLA result.
Any incomplete collection prevents Complete even when the observed subset meets the target. Do not claim a short window burn rate without separate windows and denominators.
Recommendations to freeze releases, change alerts or adjust an SLO are drafts. No release system, monitor or target is changed.
limitations: Telemetry sampling weights are estimates of represented events and do not prove full traffic capture. Ingestion delay, workspace scope and instrumentation gaps must be assessed.
A request success field is a technical indicator, not necessarily a successful business transaction. Eligibility, exclusions and the target require customer agreement.

approval.artifact: Private SLO evidence JSON and sanitized customer summary draft
approval.reason: Evidence reads require approved scope. SLO changes, alerts, release restrictions, scheduling and delivery require separate approval.

validation_cases: Healthy: synthetic 10000 events, 9950 good, zero unknown and target0.99 yield SLI0.995 and50 remaining bad events within floating point tolerance.
Finding: 9800 good out of10000 at target0.99 exhausts the budget and returns Needs attention with negative remaining budget.
Missing: zero traffic, unknown success values, denied query or incomplete collection must never produce an unqualified successful assessment.

objective: Prepare an isolated recovery drill and assess actual restore, application readiness and data integrity evidence against approved recovery objectives. Never perform a restore automatically.

inputs.name: approved_scope
inputs.description: $SUB, $RG, $VAULT, $CONTAINER, $ITEM and $JOB_ID identify exact approved Recovery Services Azure VM backup evidence. The initial collector covers Azure VM backups, not every Azure Backup workload.

inputs.name: approved_drill
inputs.description: Signed off isolated destination, restore point, network isolation, application validation, integrity checks, recovery time and recovery point targets, recovery operator, cost acceptance, stop conditions, cleanup and recovery plan. A separate authorized operator executes any drill.

inputs.name: normalized_evidence
inputs.description: $INPUT follows the bundled synthetic example and operational-evidence.md. Provide the operator drill log, recovery start, application ready, simulated loss reference and latest verified recovered committed write timestamps. A job Completed value alone does not populate application or integrity results.

permissions.role: Backup Reader or equivalent metadata read permission
permissions.scope: Only the approved Recovery Services vault and protected item
permissions.purpose: Read recovery point and completed job metadata without initiating or stopping a job
Read supplied readiness and integrity evidence; execution and restore permissions are separately approved

collection.name: Read available recovery points for the exact VM item
collection.command: az backup recoverypoint list --subscription $SUB --resource-group $RG --vault-name $VAULT --container-name $CONTAINER --item-name $ITEM --backup-management-type AzureIaasVM --output json
collection.explanation: Read metadata only. Select the correct protected item and preserve any continuation or time filtering limits. Do not substitute the newest backup time for the latest verified recovered committed write.

collection.name: Read a separately authorized restore job
collection.explanation: Run only when a real, separately authorized job ID exists. If no drill has occurred, report Not assessed and produce the drill plan, not fictional completion evidence. This command does not start, stop or wait indefinitely on a job.

collection.name: Assess timed recovery and integrity evidence locally
collection.command: python tools/operational_analysis.py --scenario backup-restore-validation --input $INPUT --contract references/output-contract.json --output restore-private-result.json --sharing-output restore-sharing-draft.json
collection.explanation: Use [the input contract](./operational-evidence.md) and [synthetic fixture](./evidence-example.json). The collector and analyzer do not execute restore commands. Verify the operator log independently before entering booleans or timestamps.

analysis: Require evidence of an isolated target, actual restore outcome and application specific integrity checks. A completed platform restore is not proof of business recovery.

Measure the drill RTO interval from the approved recovery start through application readiness, including dependent recovery steps. State whether detection and decision time are included; do not imply they were measured when the clock starts later.

Measure recovered data age from the agreed simulated loss reference minus the latest verified recovered committed write. Reject reversed timestamps and distinguish this measured drill RPO from configured backup frequency.

Compare measured seconds against customer approved targets. Failed completion, a nonisolated destination or failed integrity yields Needs attention. Missing timed or integrity evidence remains Not assessed.
Generate a drill plan, validation checklist and cleanup proposal before any execution. Restore, failover, isolation changes, integrity test writes and deletion require separate explicit approval.
limitations: The read commands cover Recovery Services Azure VM backups. Database, Backup vault and other protection types need their documented metadata adapter and service specific recovery procedure.
A single successful drill establishes only the tested data, application version, restore point, dependencies and observation window. It is not a universal recovery guarantee.

approval.artifact: Isolated restore drill plan, operator approval record and private recovery evidence
approval.reason: This workflow only prepares a drill and analyzes supplied outcomes. Actual restore, provisioning, recovery tests, cleanup and customer delivery are separately authorized.

validation_cases: Healthy: completed isolated restore, passed integrity,1200 second recovery and120 second recovered data age meet synthetic targets1800 and300 seconds.
Finding: failed integrity, incomplete restore or elapsed time above a target produces Needs attention, not backup compliant.
Missing: backup policy or Completed job without application ready and verified recovered write evidence is Not assessed.

objective: Compare approved release cohorts for error and latency regression, preserving sample coverage and uncertainty without automatically promoting or rolling back a release.

inputs.name: approved_scope
inputs.description: $SUB, $WORKSPACE, $APP_ID and UTC $START/$END identify the approved application telemetry. Validate identifiers before interpolation. $RELEASE_MANIFEST is an existing operator approved local JSON file recording release ID, version, rollout times and cohort mapping.

inputs.name: comparison_definition
inputs.description: Approved baseline and current cohorts, equal or justified comparable windows, success definition, sampling policy, minimum request count and maximum error increase in percentage points and latency increase in percent. Do not average existing percentiles.

inputs.name: normalized_evidence
inputs.description: $INPUT follows evidence-example.json. Normalize per cohort requests, failed_requests and p95_latency_ms from comparable request level evidence. comparable_cohorts=true requires operator validation of workload mix, duration, instrumentation and release mapping, not a guess.

permissions.role: Log Analytics Reader or equivalent approved query permission
permissions.scope: Approved workspace and application evidence only
permissions.purpose: Read request telemetry without repository credentials or write access to the release system

collection.name: Read request counts and latency by observed application version
collection.command:
$KQL = "AppRequests | where TimeGenerated >= datetime($START) and TimeGenerated < datetime($END) | where _ResourceId =~ '$APP_ID' | summarize requests=sum(ItemCount), failed_requests=sumif(ItemCount, Success == false), unknown_events=sumif(ItemCount, isnull(Success)), observed_p95_ms=percentile(DurationMs,95) by AppVersion"
az monitor log-analytics query --subscription $SUB --workspace $WORKSPACE --analytics-query $KQL --timespan "$START/$END" --output json
collection.explanation: AppVersion must actually identify the release or be joined to the approved manifest. This query gives a percentile of retained telemetry rows, not a sampling corrected population percentile. Use unsampled request evidence or an explicitly validated common sampling regime for comparison. Reject unknown success records and mixed version cohorts; blank AppVersion is not a known release.

collection.name: Read the approved local release mapping
collection.explanation: This is a declared required operator input, not an assumed bundled file. Resolve before and after windows or simultaneous canary and control cohorts. Record other configuration, traffic, dependency and instrumentation changes as confounders.

collection.name: Assess cohort differences locally
collection.command: python tools/operational_analysis.py --scenario release-regression-detection --input $INPUT --contract references/output-contract.json --output release-private-result.json --sharing-output release-sharing-draft.json
collection.explanation: Use [input definitions](./operational-evidence.md) and [synthetic example](./evidence-example.json). This tool reads local normalized evidence only. It never invokes a pipeline, changes traffic or performs rollback.

analysis: Require positive request denominators, the approved minimum sample per cohort and a positive baseline latency. Missing or incomparable cohorts are Not assessed.
Compute error rates independently per cohort. Error increase in percentage points is100 times (current rate minus baseline rate), not relative percent growth.
Compute latency increase percent as100 times (current p95 divided by baseline p95 minus1). Compare both values against separately configured customer thresholds.
A threshold breach recommends investigation or a pause for human review. No breach means only no configured regression observed, not approval to promote or proof of release safety.
Preserve cohort selection, observation windows, telemetry coverage and confounders. Temporal association does not establish a deployment as the cause.
limitations: Aggregate counters alone do not establish statistical significance, causal attribution or whether a critical low traffic route regressed.
Sampled percentiles, mismatched request mix and missing version instrumentation can make the comparison invalid. No automatic rollback or promotion is implemented.

approval.artifact: Release cohort evidence and nonexecuted continue, pause or investigation recommendation
approval.reason: Promotion, traffic changes, rollback, pipeline edits, scheduling and external sharing require separate explicit approval.

validation_cases: Healthy: comparable cohorts with the approved minimum sample and differences below both thresholds produce Observed, not automatic promotion.
Finding: current failures60 of1200 versus baseline10 of1000 exceed a synthetic1 percentage point threshold and require review.
Missing: insufficient requests, zero baseline latency, unknown success, unmapped version or incomparable cohorts cannot be a successful gate.

objective: Investigate application pod symptoms using scoped Kubernetes evidence, distinguishing current symptoms and recent restart events from proven root cause.

inputs.name: approved_scope
inputs.description: $SUB and $CLUSTER_ID are the approved AKS resource; $CONTEXT is an already authorized, operator verified kubeconfig context for that exact cluster, $NS an approved namespace and $POD/$CONTAINER an exact selected workload container. This workflow never obtains admin credentials or changes context.

inputs.name: window_and_thresholds
inputs.description: Approved UTC observation start/end and restart threshold. Supply two pod snapshots from the same window and match by immutable pod UID and container identity, not reused pod name.

inputs.name: normalized_evidence
inputs.description: $INPUT follows the example contract. Supply one row per unique pod with name,uid,phase,ready,waiting_reason,restart_delta and recent_oom_kills. Aggregate container and init container evidence explicitly; an empty waiting reason is known not waiting, while missing status is unassessed.

permissions.scope: Approved context, namespace, pods, events and explicitly approved pod logs
permissions.purpose: Read runtime evidence. Azure Reader does not itself grant Kubernetes data plane access. Do not list Secrets or obtain cluster admin credentials.

collection.name: Read pod and event snapshots without changing the cluster
collection.command:
kubectl --context $CONTEXT --namespace $NS get pods -o json
kubectl --context $CONTEXT --namespace $NS get events -o json
collection.explanation: Capture each output separately in the approved private evidence store and repeat the pod read at the approved end of the window. Match UIDs and container names across snapshots. Retain continuation or incomplete list evidence. Do not use --all-namespaces, create a debug pod or read Secrets by default. An unverified context blocks collection.

collection.name: Read one affected pod and optionally approved previous logs
collection.command:
kubectl --context $CONTEXT --namespace $NS get pod $POD -o json
kubectl --context $CONTEXT --namespace $NS logs $POD --container $CONTAINER --previous --tail=200 --timestamps=true
collection.explanation: The logs command is optional and requires explicit log content permission. Skip it when previous logs are unavailable and retain that reason; do not swallow an access error. Logs, pod environment values and event messages can contain confidential data. Do not copy raw content into customer reports.

collection.name: Classify normalized pod symptoms locally
collection.command: python tools/operational_analysis.py --scenario aks-application-incident-triage --input $INPUT --contract references/output-contract.json --output aks-private-result.json --sharing-output aks-sharing-draft.json
collection.explanation: Follow [the normalization rules](./operational-evidence.md) and [synthetic example](./evidence-example.json). Restart delta is observed change within the window, not lifetime restartCount. Missing first snapshots, replaced UIDs or unknown termination times must not be silently converted to zero.

analysis: Separate Pending, Failed, Unknown, readiness, waiting reasons, recent OOM kills and restart delta above the customer threshold. Do not flag a successfully completed job merely because it is not ready.
Match immutable UIDs and container identities; a newly created replacement pod cannot be compared by name with a prior pod. Include init container failures and identify missing status or history.

Use CrashLoopBackOff, ImagePullBackOff, probe events and OOM evidence as symptoms that narrow hypotheses. Do not infer incorrect memory limits or image permissions without supporting configuration and logs.
A lastState terminated OOMKilled without a timestamp in the window is historical evidence, not a confirmed new incident. A ready pod is not proof that the whole application is available.
Propose the next targeted check and mitigation draft. Restarts, deletions, scaling, resource changes, debug containers, exec and network tests that create workload activity require separate approval.
limitations: Kubernetes event retention and pod replacement can remove the necessary history. Empty pod lists or denied namespace reads are Not assessed.
The local classifier assesses normalized pod observations, not dependencies, full request paths, network policy reachability or a proven root cause.

sources.title: AKS pod crash loops and targeted read diagnostics
Validate health across the complete critical flow

approval.artifact: Sanitized pod symptom summary and nonexecuted mitigation plan
approval.reason: Approved namespace reads only. Additional log access, workload mutation, debug workloads, restart, exec, scaling and customer delivery require separate approval.

validation_cases: Healthy: running ready pods without waiting reason, recent OOM or threshold breach produce no configured symptom.
Finding: CrashLoopBackOff, a recent OOM event or restart delta above threshold produces Needs attention with symptom counts, not claimed root cause.
Missing: empty list, denied read, unknown readiness or absent observation delta is Not assessed. Duplicate UIDs and negative deltas are rejected.

objective: Diagnose scoped Azure Service Bus queue backlog and delivery failures from metadata, completion telemetry and approved dead letter reason evidence, without receiving or replaying messages.

inputs.name: approved_scope
inputs.description: $SUB,$RG,$NAMESPACE,$QUEUE identify one approved Service Bus queue. $NAMESPACE_ID is its exact parent namespace ARM ID, validated against that subscription and resource group. Validate queue names and reject quotes and control characters before dimension filter interpolation. This initial adapter covers queues, not Event Hubs consumer lag or every topic subscription.

inputs.name: window_and_thresholds
inputs.description: $START/$END define a positive UTC interval and two observed queue snapshots. Customer approves backlog growth, dead letter count, transfer dead letter count and minimum completed messages thresholds.

inputs.name: metric_mapping
inputs.description: Confirm the namespace exposes CompleteMessage with Total aggregation and the EntityName dimension in live metric definitions. If unsupported or inaccessible, provide an existing approved application completion counter export instead of running the metric query. OutgoingMessages is not a substitute for completed message settlement.

inputs.name: normalized_evidence
inputs.description: $INPUT follows the synthetic example. active_start/active_end come from countDetails snapshots, completed_messages is verified successful completion count for the same entity/window, and sample_duration_seconds is actual snapshot elapsed time. Dead letter reasons come only from separately approved metadata exports, never assumed from counts.

permissions.role: Reader and Monitoring Reader or equivalent approved metadata permissions
permissions.purpose: Read queue configuration, counters and metric definitions. Message data plane access is not granted by these roles.

permissions.role: Separately approved message metadata access when needed
permissions.scope: Only the selected queue or dead letter subqueue
permissions.purpose: Use an operator supplied reason-only export; no receive, settlement, message body export or replay is performed by this workflow

collection.name: Read queue configuration and count snapshots
collection.explanation: Repeat at the approved observation end. Read countDetails.activeMessageCount, deadLetterMessageCount and transferDeadLetterMessageCount where returned. Capture UTC collection times. Preserve absent counters as unknown rather than0 and distinguish queue state, forwarding, lock, delivery count and TTL settings.

collection.name: Discover namespace metric capabilities for the exact queue
collection.explanation: Service Bus platform metrics are exposed on the namespace. Confirm the CompleteMessage counter, Total aggregation and EntityName dimension before selecting the exact queue. Never compare namespace totals with one queue. If the completion metric is unavailable, use an approved application completion counter export.

collection.name: Read approved completion telemetry
collection.command: az monitor metrics list --subscription $SUB --resource $NAMESPACE_ID --metrics CompleteMessage --start-time $START --end-time $END --interval PT1M --aggregation Total --filter "EntityName eq '$QUEUE'" --output json
collection.explanation: Run only after verifying the metric definition and exact queue dimension in the approved namespace. Sum only nonoverlapping bins for the same entity and window. CompleteMessage measures completed settlement; outgoing deliveries alone are not successful settlement. Missing metrics are not zero completions.

collection.name: Assess queue growth and delivery evidence locally
collection.command: python tools/operational_analysis.py --scenario messaging-delivery-failure-triage --input $INPUT --contract references/output-contract.json --output messaging-private-result.json --sharing-output messaging-sharing-draft.json
collection.explanation: Use [the normalization contract](./operational-evidence.md) and [synthetic queue fixture](./evidence-example.json). Review separately supplied reason metadata without exposing message bodies. The analyzer never connects to AMQP or settles, purges or resubmits messages.

analysis: Compute active backlog growth per minute as (end depth minus start depth) times60 divided by the actual observed interval seconds. Queue depth is a stock and cannot be added to completed message flow.
Compare active growth, dead letter count, transfer dead letter count and completion evidence against customer thresholds. An idle queue with no backlog does not require a positive completion count.
Correlate delivery failures with separately observed lock loss, delivery limit, TTL, filtering and forwarding evidence. Counts alone do not identify the reason or prove messages were lost.
Distinguish source transfer dead letter subqueues from destination entity failures. Missing completion data or missing counters prevents a complete local assessment.
Prepare a recovery proposal that addresses idempotency, duplicate processing, ordering, business reconciliation, canary replay, validation and stop conditions. Never purge or replay automatically.
limitations: Queue metadata and platform counters do not prove business processing success, identify every failure reason or reveal message age distribution.
This adapter does not implement Event Hubs consumer lag, Kafka offsets or topic subscription normalization. Replay and message content inspection are outside the default workflow.

approval.artifact: Queue evidence summary and nonexecuted recovery plan
approval.reason: Only approved metadata reads and local analysis are performed. Message access, receiving, settlement, replay, purge, scaling and delivery require separate explicit approval.

validation_cases: Healthy: backlog falls from100 to20 in600 seconds, no dead letter stock and observed completions meet the approved thresholds.
Finding: growing backlog, zero completions while backlog exists, or dead letter count above threshold produces Needs attention.
Missing: absent countDetails, denied entity access or missing completion telemetry cannot be interpreted as zero backlog or zero failures.

objective: Investigate Azure OpenAI inference availability, throttling, latency, token consumption and approved quality evaluation evidence without exposing prompts or automatically changing a model deployment.

inputs.name: approved_scope
inputs.description: $SUB and $AI_ID identify the exact Azure OpenAI account and selected deployment. $START/$END are UTC. Model/API version, streaming mode, deployment and client retry behavior are recorded with the evidence.

inputs.name: metric_mapping
inputs.description: $REQUEST_METRIC,$TOKEN_METRIC and $DEPLOYMENT_FILTER are operator validated metric names and exact deployment filters from live definitions. $WORKSPACE and $LATENCY_KQL are an approved workspace GUID and reviewed client latency query. Latency must have one named measurement definition and compatible populations.

inputs.name: quality_evidence
inputs.description: Existing operator approved evaluation results for a defined dataset, rubric and model/prompt version. Supply evaluated_cases and quality_passed_cases with the minimum accepted sample. Do not run inference, export prompts or create evaluation jobs automatically.

inputs.name: normalized_evidence
inputs.description: $INPUT follows evidence-example.json with comparable_cohorts, requests, failed_requests (including throttled requests), throttled_requests, p95_latency_ms, latency_definition, tokens_total and evaluation counts. Customer thresholds are explicit; fixture values are not Microsoft service guarantees.

permissions.role: Monitoring Reader or equivalent metric permission
permissions.purpose: Read metric definitions and scoped time series without invoking inference or reading keys

permissions.role: Approved workspace query and local evaluation artifact read access
permissions.scope: Only the selected telemetry and sanitized evaluation summary
permissions.purpose: Read client latency and existing quality results without prompt bodies, completions or training data

collection.name: Discover live inference metric names and dimensions
collection.explanation: Discover names, valid aggregations and deployment/status dimensions rather than hardcoding an old API shape. Record public Azure versus other cloud endpoints and service applicability. Do not call key listing or inference APIs.

collection.name: Read scoped request and token counters
collection.command:
az monitor metrics list --subscription $SUB --resource $AI_ID --metrics $REQUEST_METRIC --start-time $START --end-time $END --interval PT1M --aggregation Total --filter $DEPLOYMENT_FILTER --output json
az monitor metrics list --subscription $SUB --resource $AI_ID --metrics $TOKEN_METRIC --start-time $START --end-time $END --interval PT1M --aggregation Total --filter $DEPLOYMENT_FILTER --output json
collection.explanation: The filter must select the approved deployment and retain supported status dimensions needed to count429 and failed requests. Do not sum overlapping aggregate and split time series, different retry layers or separate models. Confirm token metric meaning before combining prompt and completion totals. Missing series are unknown.

collection.name: Read approved request level client latency evidence
collection.explanation: $LATENCY_KQL is a required operator reviewed query, restricted to the approved application/deployment and UTC interval, that returns the defined latency percentile without prompt or completion bodies. Do not compute p95 by averaging platform Average or percentile bins. Keep nonstreaming end to end latency separate from streaming time to first token.

collection.name: Analyze inference and existing evaluation evidence locally
collection.command: python tools/operational_analysis.py --scenario ai-inference-reliability-investigation --input $INPUT --contract references/output-contract.json --output ai-private-result.json --sharing-output ai-sharing-draft.json
collection.explanation: Use [input definitions](./operational-evidence.md) and [the synthetic inference fixture](./evidence-example.json). Join only comparable model/deployment/API/streaming populations and evaluation versions. The local tool does not call Foundry, create an evaluation job or claim a model specific SLA.

analysis: Require explicit cohort comparability, positive request and quality evaluation denominators, and customer approved minimum samples. Missing quality evidence prevents a complete combined inference assessment.
Calculate failed requests / total requests and throttled requests / total requests separately. Throttled requests are a subset of failed requests in this contract and must not be added twice.
Compare a correctly measured p95 against a customer threshold for one latency definition. Streaming time to first token and nonstreaming end to end duration are not interchangeable.
Calculate quality pass rate from the existing approved dataset and rubric. Distinguish model or prompt quality issues from transport errors, capacity symptoms and application retry effects.

Report token totals as observed usage, not billed cost. Recommend additional evidence or a controlled change proposal; model switching, quota requests, retry changes, evaluation runs and scaling require separate approval.
limitations: Quality is specific to the approved evaluation dataset, rubric and model/prompt version. A transport success is not proof of a useful or correct answer.
Request, token and latency definitions vary by API, streaming mode and retry layer. Platform aggregates alone cannot supply every client percentile or a valid quality score.

approval.artifact: Private inference evidence and sanitized quality and reliability summary
approval.reason: Only approved existing metrics, logs and evaluation summaries are read. Inference, evaluation jobs, model changes, quota requests, deployment edits and customer delivery require separate approval.

validation_cases: Healthy: sufficient comparable requests and evaluation cases meet every customer configured availability, throttle, latency and quality threshold.
Finding: failure rate, throttle rate, p95 or quality breach produces separately named signals and Needs attention.
Missing: no evaluation cases, absent metric dimensions, incompatible streaming modes or insufficient samples is Not assessed, not a healthy model.
